Sona Dei vs Land Acquisition Collector (Dro) on 9 February,
2023
Bench: Surya Kant, J.K. Maheshwari

1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
 Civil Appeal No.1546/2011
 Sona Dei & Ors. 
 Versus
 Land Acquisition Collector (Dro) & Ors.

With
 Civil Appeal No.1548/2011
 O R D E R

1. These two Civil Appeals have arisen out of Judgment dated 27.04.2009 passed by the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh, whereby the first appeal of the appellants and was allowed in part and the compensation in respect of their acquired land abutting village abadi, was marginally increased from Rs.7,40,000/ per acre to Rs.7,92,600/ per acre.

entities.text: High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The compensation for the acquired land which was at a distance from village abadi was determined at the rate of Rs.5,35,000/ per acre.

2. The acquired land falls within the Revenue Estate of Village Mehlana, Tehsil and District Sonepat,
i.e., in National Capital Region (NCR).
3.
The State of Haryana acquired 20.02 acres of land of Village Mehlana for the public purpose of construction of Carrier Line Channel.

The Land Acquisition Collector awarded compensation @
Rs.3,00,000/ per acre and on reference filed by the land owners under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the Reference Court enhanced the compensation @ Rs.7,40,000/ per acre for the land abutting the village abadi and Rs.5,00,000/ per acre for the remaining land.

The Award of the Reference Court was further Date: 2023.02.16 18:20:00 IST challenged before the High Court in First Appeal and vide impugned Reason:
Judgment, as noticed earlier, the compensation has been marginally increased.
Sona Dei vs Land Acquisition Collector (Dro) on 9 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156477089/
1 4.

entities.text: Sona Dei vs Land Acquisition Collector (Dro)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The High Court while evaluating the compensation has relied upon the two Sale Deeds (Exhibit `P4) dated 26072001 and (Exhibit `P9) dated 08012002.
Both the Sale Deeds were executed prior to the issuance of Notification under Section 4 of the Act on 16082002.
The High Court rightly calculated that the average value of both the Sale Deeds was Rs.18,13,650/ per acre.

The High Court, thereafter noticed that both the Sale Deeds pertained to small pieces of land measuring 7 marlas and 16 marlas respectively, hence it applied the cut of 50% and thus determined the value of the acquired land @ Rs.7,92,600/ per acre.
5. Same analogy was applied in respect of the land away from the village abadi where the compensation was increased from Rs.5,00,000/ per acre to Rs.5,35,000/ per acre.
6. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant in Civil Appeal No.1548/2011, learned Senior Additional Advocate General on behalf of the State of Haryana and perused the record.

7. The only question that falls for consideration is whether the High Court was justified in applying the cut of 50% for the purpose of determining the market value of the acquired land?
8.

Although it is an admitted fact that the acquired land is recorded as agricultural in the revenue record, but it can hardly be disputed that the acquired land is located in National Capital Region (NCR).

Keeping that in view, the land appears to have the potentiality to be used for institutional,
industrial, residential, commercial or any other nonagriculture purposes.

Furthermore, it is a matter of record that the land has been acquired for construction of Carrier Line Channel, i.e.,
Canal.
Keeping the very public purpose of acquisition in mind, it is not acceptable that implementation of such Project would cause 50% of the acquired land to go in waste.
That being so

,
it appears to us that the High Court may not be justified in applying the cut of 50%.
9. The legal principles in this regard are well settled.
10. Recently, in Civil Appeal No.9362/2011 titled as Uttamrao (Dead) vs. The State of Maharashtra & Ors.

entities.text: Uttamrao (Dead) vs. The State of Maharashtra & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: we have held as follows: It is well settled in a catena of decisions by this Court that depending upon the area of the acquired land, its location, public purpose of acquisition and the condition of the land at the spot etc., a suitable deduction ranging from 10% to 70% of the market value can be imposed towards development charges.
There cannot be, in this regard, a uniform yardstick and the value of deduction will depend upon the fact situation of each case.
Applying this analogy, we find that the acquired land had already been converted into nonagricultural land as the appellant had been accorded permission to develop it as a residential colony.
The size of the acquired land is less than three and a half hectares.

The purpose of acquisition being to set up a power substation, neither was there a need to leave open space as mandatorily required for a residential colony nor was any part of the land expected to be utilized for basic amenities essential for a residential area.
The nature of the public purpose undoubtedly suggest that a substantial part of the land can be utilized for the said purpose.
In that case, there was no justification for the High Court firstly to deduct the value of the areas which the appellant had, before acquisition, earmarked as open space, and for roads.

That apart, the High Court could not have made a further deduction of 10% for the construction of roads for access to adjoining land or 5% deduction on account of Sona Dei vs Land Acquisition Collector (Dro) on 9 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156477089/
2 largeness of the properties when parcel of the acquired land does not comprise a huge area.

entities.text: Sona Dei vs Land Acquisition Collector (Dro)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We are satisfied that keeping in view the location of the land and the public purpose for which it has been acquired would, at best, can justify a deduction of 35% of the market value towards development charges.
In this regard, the deduction of 60% levied by the High Court highly excessive and is ordered to be reduced to 35%.
11. We have held that ideally the cut of 35% ought to be applied.
12. We see no reason to take a different view in this case.
Ordered accordingly.
13. The amount of compensation assessed at the rate of Rs.18,13,650/ in respect of land which is near Village abadi shall be redetermined by applying the cut of 35%.
14. Similarly, the amount of compensation in respect of land which is away from village abadi shall also be recalculated by applying the cut of 35%.
15. The appellants shall also be entitled to interest and solatium at the revised rate and in accordance with law.

16. Consequently, the appeals are allowed in part; the impugned Judgment of the High Court as well as the Award passed by the Reference Court are modified and the appellants are held entitled to compensation admissible after applying the cut of 35% on the market value of Rs.18,13,650/ of the acquired land as determined by the High Court.
17. The Reference Court at Sonepat is directed to redetermine the amount of compensation admissible to the appellants as directed above.

The Reference Court shall do the needful within one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this Order and the State of Haryana shall deposit the enhanced amount of compensation within two months thereafter and the enhanced amount of compensation shall be disturbed to the appellants without any delay.
